title: The same basic forms of behavior recur in simple programs regardless of details

fields.label: Label
fields.value: The same basic forms of behavior recur in simple programs regardless of details

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: Across the world of simple programs the same basic forms of behavior occur repeatedly almost independently of the underlying details of the rules, suggesting universal principles of overall behavior that should also apply to systems throughout nature.

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Ch. 1: The Foundations for a New Kind of Science

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: in the world of simple programs I have discovered that the same basic forms of behavior occur over and over again almost independent of underlying details.

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci A New Kind of Science claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Stephen Wolfram, A New Kind of Science (Champaign, IL: Wolfram Media, 2002), Chapter 1, “The Foundations for a New Kind of Science”; section “An Outline of Basic Ideas” (from p. 1), p. 4. Scope: simple programs of many types (cellular automata, Turing machines, substitution systems, etc.) and, by extension, natural systems

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on wolfram2002-ch01-05: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.60

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The computational recurrence can be evaluated across substantial public catalogs. The universality and natural-world extension remain only partly testable because classifications are interpretation-dependent and natural coverage is limited.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Enumerate multiple program formalisms and cluster trajectories using preregistered behavioral features, then test whether a small set of clusters recurs independently of rule representation. Separately compare those clusters with measured natural dynamics; recurrence in programs alone does not establish applicability to nature.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Basic forms depend on the chosen features and clustering.

The extension from programs to natural systems requires separate observational evidence.

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The asserted finding is that the same overall forms recur across simple programs almost independently of the rule details. Those families are small enough to sample with ordinary simulators, and the book's diagrams fix the conventions. The hedged remark about nature is not the decision criterion for this computational statement. Fuzzy class edges lower operationalizability without making the comparison unrunnable.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Fix four behavior classes (uniform or periodic, nested, apparently random, and localized structures) and apply them to samples of cellular automata, Turing machines, substitution systems, tag systems, and register machines. The claim is confirmed if the same classes recur across families, and refuted if some standard family produces a robustly new kind of overall behavior.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
The suggestion that the same classes govern nature is a further empirical claim and is not settled by the program survey.

Class boundaries, especially between randomness and localized structure, move with the chosen statistics.
